### Technical Setup

**Development environment setup:**

**Step 1: Install required tools**
```bash
# Install Homebrew (macOS)
/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)"

# Install Node.js
brew install node@18

# Install Git
brew install git

# Install VS Code
brew install --cask visual-studio-code

# Install Docker
brew install --cask docker
```

**Step 2: Clone repositories**
```bash
# Main application repository
git clone git@github.com:company/main-app.git
cd main-app
npm install

# Run the application locally
npm run dev

# You should see "Server running on http://localhost:3000"
```

**Step 3: Access internal systems**
- [ ] Request access to GitHub organization
- [ ] Request access to AWS (if needed for your role)
- [ ] Request access to database (read-only for now)
- [ ] Request access to design tools (Figma)
- [ ] Request access to project management (Jira)

**Step 4: Verify setup**
- [ ] Can you run the application locally?
- [ ] Can you log into all systems?
- [ ] Can you access documentation?

**Need help?** Ask in #engineering-help on Slack

---

## Week 1: Learning the Basics

### Goals for Week 1

**By the end of your first week, you should:**
- [ ] Understand our product and how it works
- [ ] Know who's on your team and what they do
- [ ] Have your development environment fully set up
- [ ] Understand our development workflow
- [ ] Complete your first small task (documentation, bug fix, etc.)
- [ ] Attend your first team meeting
- [ ] Know where to find information and ask questions

---

### Day-by-Day Plan

**Day 1 (Monday):** Setup and orientation (see above)

**Day 2 (Tuesday):** Learn the product
- [ ] Watch product demo video ([link])
- [ ] Create a test account and use the product (30 min)
- [ ] Read the Product Requirements Document for your first project ([link])
- [ ] Meeting: Team standup (9:30 AM)
- [ ] Meeting: 1-on-1 with manager (2:00 PM)

**Day 3 (Wednesday):** Learn the codebase
- [ ] Read architecture documentation ([link])
- [ ] Read coding standards ([link])
- [ ] Follow "New Engineer Code Tour" ([link])
- [ ] Pick a small "good first issue" from the backlog
- [ ] Pair with a teammate on their current work

**Day 4 (Thursday):** Start contributing
- [ ] Work on your "good first issue" (documentation update, small bug fix)
- [ ] Create your first pull request
- [ ] Attend team planning meeting (2:00 PM)
- [ ] Code review 101 - shadow a teammate doing code review

**Day 5 (Friday):** Wrap up and reflect
- [ ] Complete and merge your first PR
- [ ] Meeting: End-of-week check-in with manager
- [ ] Meeting: Team retrospective (if scheduled)
- [ ] Write down questions for next week
- [ ] Celebrate your first week! 🎉

---

### Key Meetings (Week 1)

| Meeting | When | Who | Purpose |
|---------|------|-----|---------|
| Daily Standup | M-F, 9:30 AM | Whole team | Daily sync: what you're working on, blockers |
| 1-on-1 with Manager | Tuesday, 2:00 PM | You + Manager | Check-in, answer questions, discuss goals |
| Team Planning | Thursday, 2:00 PM | Whole team | Plan next sprint's work |
| End-of-Week Check-in | Friday, 4:00 PM | You + Manager | Reflect on week 1, plan week 2 |

## Week 2-4: Building Competence

### Week 2 Goals

**This week, focus on:**
- [ ] Start working on your first substantial task/feature
- [ ] Attend all team ceremonies (standup, planning, retro)
- [ ] Meet with 3-5 people outside your immediate team (use [meeting schedule template])
- [ ] Contribute to team discussions (don't be shy!)
- [ ] Ask for code reviews and learn from feedback

**Project:** [Your first project name and description]

---

### Week 3 Goals

**This week, focus on:**
- [ ] Make significant progress on your first project (aim for 50% complete)
- [ ] Participate actively in code reviews (review others' code)
- [ ] Present your work at team demo/standup
- [ ] Identify areas where you need more learning/context
- [ ] Schedule 1-on-1s with adjacent teams (Design, Product, QA)

---

### Week 4 Goals

**This week, focus on:**
- [ ] Complete your first significant project
- [ ] Demo your work to the team
- [ ] Write documentation for what you built
- [ ] Reflect on what you've learned
- [ ] Identify what you want to learn next
- [ ] 30-day check-in with manager

---

## 30-60-90 Day Goals

### 30 Days: Learning and Contributing

**By day 30, you should:**
- [ ] Completed at least one significant feature or project
- [ ] Understand our development workflow and processes
- [ ] Know how to find information and get unblocked
- [ ] Actively participating in team meetings and discussions
- [ ] Established working relationships with team members
- [ ] Received and incorporated feedback from code reviews

**Deliverable:** Complete first project and demo to team

---

### 60 Days: Building Confidence

**By day 60, you should:**
- [ ] Working independently on tasks with minimal guidance
- [ ] Contributing to planning and estimation
- [ ] Helping with code reviews for other team members
- [ ] Understanding how your work fits into the bigger picture
- [ ] Identifying and suggesting improvements
- [ ] Building relationships beyond your immediate team

**Deliverable:** Shipped 2-3 features to production

---

### 90 Days: Full Speed

**By day 90, you should:**
- [ ] Fully productive team member
- [ ] Taking ownership of larger features/projects
- [ ] Mentoring newer team members
- [ ] Contributing to architectural decisions
- [ ] Identifying and driving improvements to team processes
- [ ] Clear on your growth path and next steps

**Deliverable:** Lead a project from requirements to deployment

**90-day review:** Formal review with manager, feedback, set goals for next quarter

### Getting Help

**When you're stuck:**

**It's okay to ask questions!** Everyone was new once. We'd rather you ask than stay stuck.

## FAQs

**Q: What should I work on first?**  
A: Your manager will assign you a "good first issue" - usually a small bug fix or documentation update. This helps you learn the codebase and development workflow with low risk.

**Q: How do I ask for help without seeming incompetent?**  
A: Asking questions is a sign of learning, not incompetence! We expect you to ask lots of questions in your first few weeks. Format: "I'm trying to [X], I've tried [Y and Z], I'm stuck on [specific issue], can you help?"

**Q: What are the working hours?**  
A: Core hours are 10 AM - 4 PM (be available for meetings). Otherwise flexible. Most people work 9-5 or 10-6. Work-life balance is important here.

**Q: Can I work from home?**  
A: [Company WFH policy]. Generally we encourage new hires to be in office first 2-4 weeks to meet people, then [X days/week remote].

**Q: When will I feel productive?**  
A: Most people feel somewhat productive by week 2-3, confident by month 2, and fully productive by month 3. It's normal to feel overwhelmed at first!

**Q: What if I don't understand the codebase?**  
A: No one understands the entire codebase! It's large and complex. You'll learn the parts relevant to your work over time. Ask teammates to explain, read code, use debugger.

**Q: How often should I commit/push code?**  
A: Commit often (multiple times per day), push at least once per day. Keep PRs small (easier to review). See [Git workflow guide](link).

**Q: What if I make a mistake?**  
A: You will make mistakes - everyone does. We have safeguards (code review, testing, staging environment). The worst that happens is we learn and improve our processes. Own it, fix it, learn from it.

**Q: Who decides what I work on?**  
A: Your manager and Product Manager prioritize work. In your first weeks, you'll work on assigned tasks. As you ramp up, you'll have more input into what you work on.

**Q: When is my first performance review?**  
A: Informal check-ins at 30, 60, 90 days. Formal review at 6 months, then annually.
